title: White Noise community signal data
body:
White Noise community signal data

116 touchpoints in 6 months. 58 GitHub issues. 58 community chat messages. All three of the same topics.

I appreciate that the team is spending real time answering the same questions while simultaneously trying to build. This report breaks down what those questions are, what the answers are, and exactly where to put them so the team stops being the first line of support.

Part 1: top 3 issues by volume (last 6 months)

Issue | GitHub issues | Chat messages | Total -- | -- | -- | -- Can't add someone to a group / keypackage errors | 23 (10 open, 13 closed) | ~28 messages | ~51 Messages and notifications not getting through | 21 (7 open, 14 closed) | ~18 messages | ~39 What files can I send / what are the size limits | 14 (6 open, 8 closed) | ~12 messages | ~26

Part 2: canned responses

1. Can't add someone to a group / getting an error when inviting someone

Thanks for flagging this. While we work on a permanent fix, here's what resolves it in most cases.

Go to Developer Settings and find Keypackage Management. You should have two keypackages, not more. If you have more than two, tap Delete Legacy to clean them up, then try the invite again.

Make sure you're on the latest version from Zapstore before trying again.

If it still doesn't work after that, reply here with your logs and we'll take a look directly.

This is a known issue and it's actively being worked on. We'll update here when it's resolved.

2. Messages not getting through / people in my group aren't receiving messages

Thanks for letting us know. Before we dig in, try these two things first.

Check your connection. A weak or dropped connection is the most common reason messages don't deliver and it usually fixes itself.

Make sure everyone in the group is on the same version of the app. A version mismatch between users will cause messages to drop silently.

If you've done both and it's still happening, reply here and describe exactly what you're seeing — which platform you're on, when it started, and whether it's affecting all messages or just some. We'll take it from there.

This is a known issue and it's actively being worked on. We'll update here when it's resolved.

3. What files can I send / what's the size limit

Here's what's currently supported.

You can send images and videos in any chat. This is not video calling — it's sending video files end to end encrypted.

The file size limit is around 100MB but it depends on your blossom server. If you're using Primal's server it's closer to 25MB, so if a file fails that's likely why.

P2P file sharing isn't available. It would require both people to be online at the same time, which White Noise doesn't require.

PDFs, audio files, and arbitrary file types are on the roadmap and coming soon.

This is a known issue and it's actively being worked on. We'll update here when it's resolved.

Part 3: where to put these answers

1. Pin one message in the community chat

The content already exists. The problem is people aren't finding it before they ask. One pinned message at the top of the chat is all it takes.

Before you ask, check the FAQ first: [link]. It covers the most common issues including group invite errors, message delivery, and file size limits.

2. Add a checkbox to every GitHub issue template

When someone opens a new issue, the first thing they see should be:

- [ ] I have checked the FAQ and my issue is not listed there: [link]

One line. Added once. Filters out the repetitive issues before they land in the team's inbox.

3. Send a welcome message to every new chat member

Most of these questions are coming from new users. Get ahead of it before the question even forms.

Hey, welcome to White Noise! Before you run into anything, check our FAQ here: [link]. It covers the most common issues people hit. If your question isn't there, feel free to ask.

I hope that this analysis has been helpful to you and the team, and that implementing these quick fixes will help you guys to get a lot of your time back so that you can focus on what matters most, and that's building. I know that you guys are working super hard to fix all of these at the development level, but in the meantime, this could reduce your customer support.

— Mo

title: Add foreground resume catch-up and snapshot refresh handling
body:
## Summary
- Added a new `Whitenoise::resume_after_background()` primitive for app foreground resume and notification tap handoff.
- The method refreshes subscriptions with bounded replay semantics, logs and skips non-catastrophic per-account failures, and replays current DB snapshots to active chat-list and message streams where possible.
- Added companion snapshot APIs for exact UI replacement: `fetch_chat_list_snapshot()` and `fetch_archived_chat_list_snapshot()`.
- Introduced `SnapshotRefresh` update triggers so Flutter can upsert refreshed rows instead of treating them as brand-new items.

## Testing
- Added focused unit coverage for idempotent resume, partial failure tolerance, snapshot rereads, and replay delivery to active chat-list/message subscribers.
- `just test-unit` passed.
- `just check` passed.
- `just coverage` was attempted, but it failed in the instrumented test harness after local relay containers became unreachable, producing broad relay-connection failures unrelated to the new foreground-resume path.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Foreground resume now refreshes subscriptions and replays chat-list snapshots to active subscribers.
  * Added snapshot fetch endpoints for active and archived chat lists.
  * Ability to enumerate currently-active subscription keys/pubkeys.

* **Improvements**
  * Preserve existing account state during same-spec subscription updates to avoid unnecessary removals.
  * Option to refresh account subscriptions without full deactivation.

* **Tests**
  * Added tests covering resume, snapshot replay, subscription enumeration, and related edge cases.

title: [codex] Backfill canonical key packages during maintenance
body:
## Summary
- require login key package setup to see a live canonical kind:30443 before treating relay state as healthy
- make key package maintenance republish a 30443 + 443 pair when live tracked state is legacy-only
- tighten scheduler integration coverage so maintenance publish and rotation assert both twins

## Root Cause
Maintenance and login could treat a tracked legacy kind:443 key package as fully healthy. That let production recovery paths leave an account without the canonical D-tagged kind:30443 twin while local MLS material still existed.

## Validation
- `PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" just int-test scheduler`
- `PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" just precommit-quick`

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Prevents maintenance from leaving only legacy key packages; ensures a canonical key package is published or preserved so accounts aren’t treated as fresh.
  * Tightens health checks so legacy-only relay state is no longer considered healthy and triggers republish when needed.

* **Tests**
  * Added tests validating republish behavior, stricter rotation completion, and preservation of canonical+legacy pairs.

* **Refactor**
  * Clarified rotation/publish decision logic and added helpers to detect canonical vs legacy package states.
